cases.title: Verify editing Cost on the Receive Parts screen updates the Sell price
cases.permissions_required: Receive access + See Financial Data (cost/sell fields).
preconditions: 1. Signed in as Admin on the staging build.

2. First check the shop's pricing settings: note whether the part's category has a pricing rule (markup/margin) that turns a cost into a sell price. If the shop's pricing setup genuinely says the sell price should be zero, this test does not apply — note that and stop.
3. A work order has an ordered part waiting to be received, with an editable Cost on the Receive Parts screen (for example a Vendor Missing part with Cost still at $0).
steps: 1. Open the Receive Parts screen for the work order's purchase order.
2. Note the current value in the Sell field for the part.
3. Enter a real cost (for example 50) in the Cost field for the part and click away so the value saves.
4. Look at the Sell field for the same part again.
expected: 1. After the Cost is entered, the Sell price updates to follow the shop's pricing rules — it is calculated from the new cost.
2. The Sell price must NOT stay at 0 after a real cost has been entered (unless the shop's pricing setup genuinely dictates a zero sell price — see the precondition check).
3. VIU-confirm: the exact way Sell follows Cost (immediately on screen, or after saving) must be confirmed live on the build — it has not been observed yet.
cases.design_ref: None (pre-existing default behavior; no Simple Flow spec requirement). Related recorded fact: POST /api/work-orders/part/change-request recalculates sellPrice/margin (APP-ACTIONS-PLAYBOOK).
cases.notes: Born from the founder's (Fabian) 2026-07-29 report: Sell stayed 0 on WO S3-25982's Receive Parts screen no matter how many times Cost was updated. Our nearest existing cases (SF-VEND-06/C29442, SF-RCV-06/C29374, SF-BULK-06/C29355, SF-RCV-10/C29440, SF-VAL-09/C29423) only assert that cost/sell are PRESENT/editable/locked — none assert that Sell recalculates when Cost changes.

cases.title: Verify repeated Cost edits on the Receive Parts screen each update the Sell price
cases.permissions_required: Receive access + See Financial Data (cost/sell fields).
preconditions: 1. Same setup as the single-edit case: pricing settings checked first, and a part on the Receive Parts screen with an editable Cost.
2. The single-edit behavior (Cost updates Sell once) already works — run that case first.
steps: 1. On the Receive Parts screen, enter a cost (for example 50) and note the resulting Sell price.
2. Change the Cost again to a clearly different value (for example 100) and click away.
4. Change the Cost a third time (for example back to 50) and check the Sell price once more.
expected: 1. Every cost change produces a matching updated Sell price — the second and third edits recalculate just like the first.
2. The Sell price never gets stuck at an old value (or at 0) after any of the repeated edits.
3. Setting the same cost again (step 4) gives back the same sell price as before — the calculation is consistent.
cases.design_ref: None (pre-existing default behavior). The founder's report specifically says 'no matter how many times the Cost price is updated' — this case covers the repeat-edit half of that report.
cases.notes: Companion to SF-RCV-14; kept separate because a first-edit-works / later-edits-stuck bug is a real and distinct failure mode.

cases.title: Verify editing Cost in the part edit dialog updates the Sell price and Margin
cases.permissions_required: WO Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
preconditions: 1. Signed in as Admin on the staging build.
2. Pricing settings checked first (same check as SF-RCV-14).
3. A work order line has a part whose edit dialog can be opened (the dialog shows Part Number, Description, Quantity, Source, Vendor, Cost, Sell).
steps: 1. Open the part's edit dialog from the work order line.
3. Change the Cost to a clearly different value and save.
4. Re-open the dialog and check the Sell (and Margin, if shown) values.
expected: 1. After the cost change is saved, the Sell price (and Margin, if shown) reflect the new cost per the shop's pricing rules.

2. VIU-confirm: whether this dialog applies the same automatic cost-to-sell behavior as the Receive Parts screen has NOT been observed live yet — confirm on the build. Our recorded API fact (part change-request recalculates sellPrice/margin) suggests it does, but that was never turned into an observed test result.
